questions.question:
**Select the most appropriate idiom that can substitute the italicised words in the given sentence.**

Some people still feel that they have ***very little ***freedom to be innovative in their work.

options.text: an old head on young shoulders

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **"very little elbow room"**.

__
 
• **Words** with nearly the same meaning as **another term** are known as **synonyms**.
 
• 
 
The most appropriate idiom that can substitute the italicized words in the given sentence is elbow room.

 
 
• 
 
The idiom '**elbow room'** is used to describe having enough space to move or act.

 
 
• 
 
It implies the ability to be creative and innovative without feeling restricted or confined. It means **enough space to move freely (पर्याप्त स्‍थान - खुलकर चलने-फिरने के लिए)**

 
 
• **Example:** *There is not much **elbow room** in that train.*
 
 
 
 
 
• The word **"very little freedom" **in the sentence means **there is limited flexibility for being innovative in work.**
 
• Hence, the most appropriate substitution will be **'very little elbow room' **to match the meaning of the sentence.
 
 
• 
 
The phrase very little elbow room means: **Not enough space to move around in comfortably or freely.**

 
 
• 
 
For example, “We were tightly squashed in at dinner, with **very little elbow room.”**

 
 
 
 
• The rest of the options are not matching with the meaning of **"very little freedom".**

 

Therefore, the correct sentence is **"Some people still feel that they have *very *little ****elbow room__ to be innovative in their work."**

options.text: To be completely different from each other
To be very similar to each other
To have a close relation with another person

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **To be completely different from each other.**

__
 
• The idiom **"Be like chalk and cheese"** means two things or people that are completely different from each other. (एकदम अलग)

 
 
• **Example: **Despite being twins, John and Jake are like chalk and cheese in their personalities.
 
 
 
• **"To be completely different from each other" **refers to having no similarities at all, often in terms of characteristics, preferences, or nature. (पूरी तरह से अलग होना)
 
 
• **Example: **Her approach to solving problems is completely different from mine; we are like chalk and cheese.
 
 
 
• Hence, the idiom "Be like chalk and cheese" means to be completely different from each other.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 1** i.e. To be completely different from each other.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**
